scores.reason: Strong need-fit in source for this persona: a dedicated student audience landing ('Your projects deserve a proper introduction'), record hints covering projects/internships/volunteering/coursework, claim kinds for academic_project/volunteering/internship, and a free no-account CV-to-vacancy evidence check with real downloads. The tool reviews and aligns existing material against a pasted vacancy rather than authoring a first CV, and it explicitly refuses to verify qualifications or predict outcomes — honest, but students starting from nothing still do the writing themselves. Live usefulness is not demonstrated by this package.

Source implements low-friction entry: /check works without signup, six numbered steps with guidance, audience carried via ?audience=student, editable suggested starting roles (e.g., 'Graduate business analyst', 'Operations intern'), and a 30-minute draft recovery with a clear restore notice. Account creation is only needed for private saving/tracking. However, the cloud Job Loop is capped at a 10-account pilot with explicit pilot-full handling, so a new student may be gated; no live onboarding journey was observed.

Implemented source shows deliberate accessibility work: role=status loading regions, aria-labels/aria-current, decorative icons aria-hidden, per-step heading focus management with scrollIntoView, labelled Field/Select/Consent controls, details/summary disclosures, and titled iframes for PDF preview. But the coverage limits state layout, accessibility and mobile PDF interoperability were not observed; responsive/mobile behavior, keyboard completion of the full wizard, and screen-reader outcomes cannot be confirmed from excerpts. Partial confidence only.

This is the strongest area in source: server-side validateClaim enforces complete literal source passages preserving negation, contribution and attribution; the evidence engine distinguishes direct/partial/missing/review, detects pending coursework, weakened verbs, negation scoping and non-English text; downloads require dual fact/privacy confirmations; PDF preview is the exact byte artifact later downloaded; the evidence report is kept separate from the CV; and stale input hashes force re-review. Caveats: rendering is plain text-based layout with no demonstrated templates, and unsupported characters block PDF with DOCX/TXT fallback. Not observed live.

The reliable, implemented path is manual: the student pastes one vacancy, and assessment is an honestly-labeled heuristic ('approved-phrase-overlap-v1; heuristic relevance, not ATS or eligibility certification') with flags like EXPERIENCE_REQUIREMENT_GAP and PROJECT_AND_INTERNSHIP_CONTEXT_PRESERVED — good for internship gap analysis. Automated discovery (Tavily web search, employer feeds) requires configured API keys; matching is token-overlap heuristics on titles/locations. Actual vacancy coverage and configuration are unobserved and unknown; neither assumed working nor broken.

Automation exists in source but is consent- and configuration-gated: a rules mode using confirmed facts, optional per-run external model consent limited to claim selection, opt-in recurring schedules (weekdays/daily/weekly with timezone), Gmail draft creation only after packet approval plus recipient/attachment confirmation, and idempotent background runs. There is deliberately no auto-submit or send. For the free check, effort is mostly manual review and editing. Whether scheduler/providers are actually enabled is unobserved; realistic time savings are not established.

Source implements a coherent tracker: statuses saved→prepared→applied→interview→offer/rejected/withdrawn, follow-up dates with due/upcoming computation, next-action cards in the workspace overview, deadline requirements flagged in the evidence engine with timezone cautions, and Gmail read of recruitment inbox as an optional configured lane. Honest framing: 'The tracker records the progress you report. Opening a link does not count as a submission.' Manual status entry and unobserved live tracking mutations cap the score.

Notable implemented behavior: idempotency keys with 409 conflict when facts change, LOOP_STALE_INPUT rejection on approval after record/vacancy edits, resume/cancel run actions with honest worker-unreachable messaging, failed requests not consuming credits, 30-minute owner-bound draft recovery (memory-only by default, consented sessionStorage for refresh), account-change clearing, object-URL cleanup, ErrorBoundary and React Query retry. Recovery limits (tab close/sign-out clears unsaved work) are communicated rather than hidden. Live reliability and recovery outcomes were not observed.

Source implements unusually granular control: the free check runs client-side with no external AI; drafts stay in tab memory unless sessionStorage is consented; claims carry confirmed/shareable flags; excluded terms and discreet-search review flags exist; models receive only confirmed shareable facts plus vacancy text, not the raw CV; Gmail requires separate OAuth, drafts need explicit approval, no send capability, disconnect removes stored credentials; a privacy-request form is built in. Residual gaps: actual deployed data handling, retention and deletion execution are unobserved, and students are still advised to self-redact sensitive content.

Explicitly a persona inference, not purchase research: the capabilities a first-applicant needs most — CV check, evidence review, downloads, optional saving/tracking — are free with no card, and the pilot makes even the Job Loop free (capped at 10 accounts). Proposed tiers ($15/mo Focus, $29/mo Job Loop) are not for sale and skew toward recurring volume that suits busy professionals more than students, who are typically price-sensitive and apply in bursts. Inferred willingness to pay is therefore low-to-moderate; the free tier likely cannibalizes student payment unless recurring discovery proves indispensable.

strengths: Direct student fit: a dedicated /for-students audience, record guidance to 'start with projects, internships, volunteering and coursework', claim kinds covering academic_project/personal_project/volunteering/internship/education, a one-page CV default for students, and an explicit guarantee that no years of experience, credentials or leadership are inferred from audience choice.

Evidence integrity and anti-overclaiming: server-side claim validation requires complete literal source passages preserving negation, contribution and team attribution; the evidence engine flags pending coursework, weakened verbs (assisted/supported) and negations; external model output is restricted to claim IDs only — 'No generated factual text has been accepted.'

Genuinely free, account-optional core: the six-step CV check needs no signup or card, uses no pack credits, runs client-side without external AI, and provides exact-byte PDF preview plus PDF/DOCX/TXT downloads with a separate evidence report.

Privacy and consent architecture: in-memory 30-minute draft recovery with sessionStorage only after explicit consent, owner-bound drafts cleared on account change, per-claim shareable flags, excluded terms, discreet search, shareable-facts-only model payloads, separate Gmail OAuth with drafts requiring recipient/attachment approval, and no send or submit action.

Reliability engineering in source: idempotent run requests with hash-bound conflict detection, stale-input rejection before packet approval, resume/cancel run actions, dual fact/disclosure confirmations, draft invalidation on any edit, and honest failure messaging (e.g., worker unreachable → resume run).
weaknesses: No observed live behavior: this package is bounded source excerpts only; no authenticated run, scheduler execution, provider call, account save, or employer submission is demonstrated, and the free pilot is capped at 10 accounts (subscription-plans maxUsers: 10) with explicit pilot-full handling, so actual availability for a new student is unknown.

Document output quality is functionally plain: exports render reviewed text via jsPDF/docx with basic styling and no evidence of designed CV templates; unsupported characters hard-fail PDF generation (fallback to DOCX/TXT advised), and scanned PDFs/legacy .doc are unsupported, which affects real student files.

High manual burden by design: students must supply a CV and vacancy, review evidence, edit wording themselves, and tick dual confirmations; there is no guided CV authoring for someone writing their first CV, and English-only text analysis excludes non-English documents.

Automation value is gated: scheduler, external models, Gmail and search all require configuration and consent, none of which is demonstrated; the rules mode is implemented but its end-to-end effect on effort is unverified.

scores.reason: The core value — one reusable, source-verified career record, evidence-side-by-side review and prepared packs around a working day — is explicitly built for this persona (job-loop-audiences.ts professional entry, discreetSearch true). The free no-signup CV check delivers standalone value. However, preparation stops at review: the user still submits manually, discovery is conditional on configured providers, and time savings are asserted in copy but not demonstrated. Useful coherent experience with material gaps.

Onboarding offers a no-account six-step check, audience-specific landing pages with suggested roles, prefilled editable preferences (pageTarget 2, discreetSearch), draft recovery, and protected routes that preserve intent (MvpApp.tsx ProtectedJobLoop retains the gmail ticket). Against that, the cloud loop demands substantial upfront work — profile, source text, claim-by-claim confirmation, vacancy input — before any prepared packet, which is heavy for someone with limited search time, and first-packet time is unmeasured.

Source shows real accessibility effort: role='status' loading states, labelled fields, aria-current on audience nav, focus management and scroll-to-heading on step change, skip-target #main-content, and consent checkboxes with clear copy. But this package observes no rendered layout: mobile responsiveness, small-screen usability of the multi-panel Job Loop, iframe PDF previews on mobile, and WCAG conformance are unverified. Partial usefulness with substantial uncertainty.

Strongest area. Claims are validated against literal source passages with negation/attribution preserved and cropped quotes rejected; pending, weakened and negated wording is flagged (cv-evidence.ts PENDING/WEAKENED/NEGATIVE analysis); deadlines and eligibility conditions are classed as review items, not achievements; the PDF preview is the exact download artifact; evidence reports stay separate from the CV; external model output is accepted only as a bounded claimId selection with 'No generated factual text has been accepted' on parse failure. Genuinely conservative, inspectable document quality.

Manually pasted vacancies work and are source-linked, but breadth is unproven: employer feeds and Tavily web search exist only when configured (searchReady requires an API key; 503 LOOP_SEARCH_NOT_CONFIGURED otherwise), discovery matching is a simple ≥50% title word-overlap plus location substring heuristic, and experience-gap flags filter out discoveries. No actual vacancy coverage, source list or freshness is demonstrated. Major unmet-need risk for a professional relying on the tool to surface roles.

Automation building blocks are real: rules mode without external AI, consented Claude/OpenAI/Kimi claim selection, background runs, a weekday/daily/weekly scheduler with timezone and opt-in consent, and optional Gmail draft creation with recipient confirmation. Yet everything is gated on deployment configuration (capabilities.scheduler, model readiness, Gmail), review burden is mandatory at every step, and no scheduled run has been observed. Effort reduction is plausible but unverified and partly manual.

The workspace surfaces the next action, follow-up dues, upcoming reminders, run history and per-opportunity statuses from saved through offer/rejected/withdrawn (JobLoopPanels overview, loopFollowUpDue). Honestly, it records only user-reported progress — opening a link does not count as submission — and Gmail read summaries that could automate status detection are optional and unverified. Actionable but manual.

Designed-for-failure behavior is evident: idempotency via requestId with hash comparison and 409 conflicts, resume/cancel run actions, stale-input rejection at approval, graceful worker-dispatch degradation, ErrorBoundary and retry:1 queries, and draft recovery cleared on account change. Limitations: recovery lasts 30 minutes and dies on refresh without consent or on tab close, and none of the recovery or run behavior has been observed executing live.

Confidentiality needs are addressed structurally: discreet-search consent default for professionals with a DISCREET_SEARCH_REVIEW flag, user-managed excludedTerms, redaction of gap text against the profile, per-claim confirmed/shareable gates, models receiving only cleared facts rather than the raw CV, a separate previewed Gmail OAuth flow with disconnect semantics, no send/submit capability, owner-scoped recovery cleared on account switch, and support forms warning against including confidential data. Deletion controls exist (deleteTarget). Live verification of erasure is not in this package.

Qualified persona inference only: an employed 5–10-year professional has disposable income and acute time scarcity, so $15–$29/month tiers are plausibly within range if preparation genuinely saves hours. But checkout is disabled, tiers are explicitly 'proposals, not offers for sale', the pilot is capped at ten accounts, and the time-saving core (discovery plus scheduled preparation) is unverified. Willingness is contingent on demonstrated automation value; currently unproven and unpurchasable.
